NASB.2: 'Oh that my grief were actually weighed And laid in the balances together with my calamity!
NASB.3: 'For then it would be heavier than the sand of the seas; Therefore my words have been rash.
NASB.4: 'For the arrows of the Almighty are within me, Their poison my spirit drinks; The terrors of God are arrayed against me.
NASB.5: 'Does the wild donkey bray over [his] grass, Or does the ox low over his fodder?
NASB.6: 'Can something tasteless be eaten without salt, Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?
NASB.7: 'My soul refuses to touch [them]; They are like loathsome food to me.
NASB.8: 'Oh that my request might come to pass, And that God would grant my longing!
NASB.9: 'Would that God were willing to crush me, That He would loose His hand and cut me off!
NASB.10: 'But it is still my consolation, And I rejoice in unsparing pain, That I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
NASB.11: 'What is my strength, that I should wait? And what is my end, that I should endure?
NASB.12: 'Is my strength the strength of stones, Or is my flesh bronze?
NASB.13: 'Is it that my help is not within me, And that deliverance is driven from me?
NASB.14: 'For the despairing man [there should be] kindness from his friend; So that he does not forsake the fear of the Almighty.
NASB.15: 'My brothers have acted deceitfully like a wadi, Like the torrents of wadis which vanish,
NASB.16: Which are turbid because of ice [And] into which the snow melts.
NASB.17: 'When they become waterless, they are silent, When it is hot, they vanish from their place.
NASB.18: 'The paths of their course wind along, They go up into nothing and perish.
NASB.19: 'The caravans of Tema looked, The travelers of Sheba hoped for them.
NASB.20: 'They were disappointed for they had trusted, They came there and were confounded.
NASB.21: 'Indeed, you have now become such, You see a terror and are afraid.
NASB.22: 'Have I said, 'Give me [something],' Or, 'Offer a bribe for me from your wealth,'
NASB.23: Or, 'Deliver me from the hand of the adversary,' Or, 'Redeem me from the hand of the tyrants '?
NASB.24: 'Teach me, and I will be silent; And show me how I have erred.
NASB.25: 'How painful are honest words! But what does your argument prove?
NASB.26: 'Do you intend to reprove [my] words, When the words of one in despair belong to the wind?
NASB.27: 'You would even cast [lots] for the orphans And barter over your friend.
NASB.28: 'Now please look at me, And [see] if I lie to your face.
NASB.29: 'Desist now, let there be no injustice; Even desist, my righteousness is yet in it.
NASB.30: 'Is there injustice on my tongue? Cannot my palate discern calamities?

ESV.2: “Oh that my vexation were weighed, and all my calamity laid in the balances!
ESV.3: For then it would be heavier than the sand of the sea; therefore my words have been rash.
ESV.4: For the arrows of the Almighty are in me; my spirit drinks their poison; the terrors of God are arrayed against me.
ESV.5: Does the wild donkey bray when he has grass, or the ox low over his fodder?
ESV.6: Can that which is tasteless be eaten without salt, or is there any taste in the juice of the mallow?
ESV.7: My appetite refuses to touch them; they are as food that is loathsome to me.
ESV.8: “Oh that I might have my request, and that God would fulfill my hope,
ESV.9: that it would please God to crush me, that he would let loose his hand and cut me off!
ESV.10: This would be my comfort; I would even exult  in pain unsparing, for I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
ESV.11: What is my strength, that I should wait? And what is my end, that I should be patient?
ESV.12: Is my strength the strength of stones, or is my flesh bronze?
ESV.13: Have I any help in me, when resource is driven from me?
ESV.14: “He who withholds  kindness from a friend forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
ESV.15: My brothers are treacherous as a torrent-bed, as torrential streams that pass away,
ESV.16: which are dark with ice, and where the snow hides itself.
ESV.17: When they melt, they disappear; when it is hot, they vanish from their place.
ESV.18: The caravans turn aside from their course; they go up into the waste and perish.
ESV.19: The caravans of Tema look, the travelers of Sheba hope.
ESV.20: They are ashamed because they were confident; they come there and are disappointed.
ESV.21: For you have now become nothing; you see my calamity and are afraid.
ESV.22: Have I said, ‘Make me a gift’? Or, ‘From your wealth offer a bribe for me’?
ESV.23: Or, ‘Deliver me from the adversary's hand’? Or, ‘Redeem me from the hand of the ruthless’?
ESV.24: “Teach me, and I will be silent; make me understand how I have gone astray.
ESV.25: How forceful are upright words! But what does reproof from you reprove?
ESV.26: Do you think that you can reprove words, when the speech of a despairing man is wind?
ESV.27: You would even cast lots over the fatherless, and bargain over your friend.
ESV.28: “But now, be pleased to look at me, for I will not lie to your face.
ESV.29: Please turn; let no injustice be done. Turn now; my vindication is at stake.
ESV.30: Is there any injustice on my tongue? Cannot my palate discern the cause of calamity?

NKJV.2: “Oh, that my grief were fully weighed, And my calamity laid with it on the scales!
NKJV.3: For then it would be heavier than the sand of the sea— Therefore my words have been rash.
NKJV.4: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me; My spirit drinks in their poison; The terrors of God are arrayed against me.
NKJV.5: Does the wild donkey bray when it has grass, Or does the ox low over its fodder?
NKJV.6: Can flavorless food be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?
NKJV.7: My soul refuses to touch them; They are as loathsome food to me.
NKJV.8: “Oh, that I might have my request, That God would grant me the thing that I long for!
NKJV.9: That it would please God to crush me, That He would loose His hand and cut me off!
NKJV.10: Then I would still have comfort; Though in anguish I would exult, He will not spare; For I have not concealed the words of the Holy One.
NKJV.11: “What strength do I have, that I should hope? And what is my end, that I should prolong my life?
NKJV.12: Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh bronze?
NKJV.13: Is my help not within me? And is success driven from me?
NKJV.14: “To him who is afflicted, kindness should be shown by his friend, Even though he forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
NKJV.15: My brothers have dealt deceitfully like a brook,  Like the streams of the brooks that pass away,
NKJV.16: Which are dark because of the ice, And into which the snow vanishes.
NKJV.17: When it is warm, they cease to flow; When it is hot, they vanish from their place.
NKJV.18: The paths of their way turn aside, They go nowhere and perish.
NKJV.19: The caravans of Tema look, The travelers of Sheba hope for them.
NKJV.20: They are disappointed because they were confident; They come there and are confused.
NKJV.21: For now you are nothing, You see terror and are afraid.
NKJV.22: Did I ever say, ‘Bring something to me’? Or, ‘Offer a bribe for me from your wealth’?
NKJV.23: Or, ‘Deliver me from the enemy’s hand’? Or, ‘Redeem me from the hand of oppressors’?
NKJV.24: “Teach me, and I will hold my tongue; Cause me to understand wherein I have erred.
NKJV.25: How forceful are right words! But what does your arguing prove?
NKJV.26: Do you intend to rebuke my words, And the speeches of a desperate one, which are as wind?
NKJV.27: Yes, you overwhelm the fatherless, And you undermine your friend.
NKJV.28: Now therefore, be pleased to look at me; For I would never lie to your face.
NKJV.29: Yield now, let there be no injustice! Yes, concede, my righteousness still stands!
NKJV.30: Is there injustice on my tongue? Cannot my taste discern the unsavory?

WEB.2: “Oh that my anguish were weighed, and all my calamity laid in the balances!
WEB.3: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas, therefore have my words been rash.
WEB.4: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me. My spirit drinks up their poison. The terrors of God set themselves in array against me.
WEB.5: Does the wild donkey bray when he has grass? Or does the ox low over his fodder?
WEB.6: Can that which has no flavor be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?
WEB.7: My soul refuses to touch them. They are as loathsome food to me.
WEB.8: “Oh that I might have my request, that God would grant the thing that I long for,
WEB.9: even that it would please God to crush me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!
WEB.10: Be it still my consolation, yes, let me exult in pain that doesn’t spare, that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
WEB.11: What is my strength, that I should wait? What is my end, that I should be patient?
WEB.12: Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of brass?
WEB.13: Isn’t it that I have no help in me, That wisdom is driven quite from me?
WEB.14: “To him who is ready to faint, kindness should be shown from his friend; even to him who forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
WEB.15: My brothers have dealt deceitfully as a brook, as the channel of brooks that pass away;
WEB.16: Which are black by reason of the ice, in which the snow hides itself.
WEB.17: In the dry season, they vanish. When it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.
WEB.18: The caravans that travel beside them turn aside. They go up into the waste, and perish.
WEB.19: The caravans of Tema looked. The companies of Sheba waited for them.
WEB.20: They were distressed because they were confident. They came there, and were confounded.
WEB.21: For now you are nothing. You see a terror, and are afraid.
WEB.22: Did I say, ‘Give to me?’ or, ‘Offer a present for me from your substance?’
WEB.23: or, ‘Deliver me from the adversary’s hand?’ or, ‘Redeem me from the hand of the oppressors?’
WEB.24: “Teach me, and I will hold my peace. Cause me to understand wherein I have erred.
WEB.25: How forcible are words of uprightness! But your reproof, what does it reprove?
WEB.26: Do you intend to reprove words, since the speeches of one who is desperate are as wind?
WEB.27: Yes, you would even cast lots for the fatherless, and make merchandise of your friend.
WEB.28: Now therefore be pleased to look at me, for surely I shall not lie to your face.
WEB.29: Please return. Let there be no injustice. Yes, return again. My cause is righteous.
WEB.30: Is there injustice on my tongue? Can’t my taste discern mischievous things?

NLT.2:
“If my misery could be weighed
and my troubles be put on the scales,
NLT.3:
they would outweigh all the sands of the sea.
That is why I spoke impulsively.
NLT.4:
For the Almighty has struck me down with his arrows.
Their poison infects my spirit.
God’s terrors are lined up against me.
NLT.5:
Don’t I have a right to complain?
Don’t wild donkeys bray when they find no grass,
and oxen bellow when they have no food?
NLT.6:
Don’t people complain about unsalted food?
Does anyone want the tasteless white of an egg?
NLT.7:
My appetite disappears when I look at it;
I gag at the thought of eating it!
NLT.8:
“Oh, that I might have my request,
that God would grant my desire.
NLT.9:
I wish he would crush me.
I wish he would reach out his hand and kill me.
NLT.10:
At least I can take comfort in this:
Despite the pain,
I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
NLT.11:
But I don’t have the strength to endure.
I have nothing to live for.
NLT.12:
Do I have the strength of a stone?
Is my body made of bronze?
NLT.13:
No, I am utterly helpless,
without any chance of success.
NLT.14:
“One should be kind to a fainting friend,
but you accuse me without any fear of the Almighty.
NLT.15:
My brothers, you have proved as unreliable as a seasonal brook
that overflows its banks in the spring
NLT.16: when it is swollen with ice and melting snow.
NLT.17:
But when the hot weather arrives, the water disappears.
The brook vanishes in the heat.
NLT.18:
The caravans turn aside to be refreshed,
but there is nothing to drink, so they die.
NLT.19:
The caravans from Tema search for this water;
the travelers from Sheba hope to find it.
NLT.20:
They count on it but are disappointed.
When they arrive, their hopes are dashed.
NLT.21:
You, too, have given no help.
You have seen my calamity, and you are afraid.
NLT.22:
But why? Have I ever asked you for a gift?
Have I begged for anything of yours for myself?
NLT.23:
Have I asked you to rescue me from my enemies,
or to save me from ruthless people?
NLT.24:
Teach me, and I will keep quiet.
Show me what I have done wrong.
NLT.25:
Honest words can be painful,
but what do your criticisms amount to?
NLT.26:
Do you think your words are convincing
when you disregard my cry of desperation?
NLT.27:
You would even send an orphan into slavery
or sell a friend.
NLT.28:
Look at me!
Would I lie to your face?
NLT.29:
Stop assuming my guilt,
for I have done no wrong.
NLT.30:
Do you think I am lying?
Don’t I know the difference between right and wrong?

AMP.2:
"Oh, that my grief could actually be weighed
And placed in the balances together with my tragedy [to see if my grief is the grief of a coward]!
AMP.3:
"For now it would be heavier than the sand of the sea;
Therefore my words have been incoherent,
AMP.4:
Because the arrows of the Almighty are within me,
My spirit drinks their poison;
The terrors of God are arrayed against me.
AMP.5:
"Does the wild donkey bray when he has grass?
Or does the ox low over his fodder?
AMP.6:
"Can something that has no taste to it be eaten without salt?
Or is there any flavor in the white of an egg?
AMP.7:
"My soul refuses to touch them;
Such things are like loathsome food to me [sickening and repugnant].
AMP.8:
"Oh that my request would come to pass,
And that God would grant me the thing that I long for!
AMP.9:
"I wish that it would please God to crush me,
That He would let loose His hand and cut me off.
AMP.10:
"Then I would still have consolation,
And I would jump for joy amid unsparing pain,
That I have not denied or hidden the words of the Holy One.
AMP.11:
"What strength do I have left, that I should wait [and hope]?
And what is ahead of me, that I should be patient and endure?
AMP.12:
"Is my strength and endurance that of stones,
Or is my flesh made of bronze?
AMP.13:
"Is it that I have no help within myself,
And that success and wisdom have been driven from me?
AMP.14:
"For the despairing man there should be kindness from his friend;
So that he does not abandon (turn away from) the fear of the Almighty.
AMP.15:
"My brothers have acted deceitfully like a brook,
Like the torrents of brooks that vanish,
AMP.16:
Which are dull and dirty because of ice,
And into which the snow melts and hides itself;
AMP.17:
When it is warm, they are silent and cease to flow;
When it is hot, they vanish from their place.
AMP.18:
"The paths of their course wind along,
They go up into nothing and perish.
[Your counsel is as helpful to me as a dry streambed in the heat of summer.]
AMP.19:
"The caravans of Tema looked [for water],
The caravans of Sheba waited for them [in vain].
AMP.20:
"They were put to shame and disappointed because they had trusted [that they would find water];
They came there and were ashamed.
AMP.21:
"Indeed, you have now become like a dried-up stream,
You see a terror [believing me to be a victim of the wrath of God] and are afraid [to be compassionate].
AMP.22:
"Did I ever say, 'Give me something,'
Or, 'Pay a bribe for me from your wealth,'
AMP.23:
Or, 'Rescue me from the adversary's hand,'
Or, 'Redeem me from the hand of the tyrants'?
AMP.24:
"Teach me, and I will be silent;
And show me how I have erred.
AMP.25:
"How painful are words of honesty.
But what does your argument prove?
AMP.26:
"Do you intend to reprove my words [with a convincing argument],
When the words of one in despair belong to the wind [and go ignored]?
AMP.27:
"You would cast lots (gamble) over the fatherless
And bargain away your friend.
AMP.28:
"Now please look at me,
And see if I lie to your face [for you know that I would not].
AMP.29:
"Turn away [from your suspicion], let there be no injustice;
Turn away, my righteousness and vindication is still in it.
AMP.30:
"Is there injustice or malice on my tongue?
Can my palate not discern what is destructive?

But what does your rebuke prove?
CSB17.26:
Do you think that you can disprove my words
or that a despairing man’s words are mere wind? ⓘ
CSB17.27:
No doubt you would cast lots for a fatherless child

MSG.2:
"If my misery could be weighed,
if you could pile the whole bitter load on the scales,
MSG.3:
It would be heavier than all the sand of the sea!
Is it any wonder that I'm screaming like a caged cat?
MSG.4:
The arrows of God Almighty are in me,
poison arrows—and I'm poisoned all through!
God has dumped the whole works on me.
MSG.5:
Donkeys bray and cows moo when they run out of pasture—
so don't expect me to keep quiet in this.
MSG.6:
Do you see what God has dished out for me?
It's enough to turn anyone's stomach!
MSG.7:
Everything in me is repulsed by it—
it makes me sick.
MSG.8:
"All I want is an answer to one prayer,
a last request to be honored:
MSG.9:
Let God step on me—squash me like a bug,
and be done with me for good.
MSG.10:
I'd at least have the satisfaction
of not having blasphemed the Holy God,
before being pressed past the limits.
MSG.11:
Where's the strength to keep my hopes up?
What future do I have to keep me going?
MSG.12:
Do you think I have nerves of steel?
Do you think I'm made of iron?
MSG.13:
Do you think I can pull myself up by my bootstraps?
Why, I don't even have any boots!
MSG.14:
"When desperate people give up on God Almighty,
their friends, at least, should stick with them.
MSG.15:
But my brothers are fickle as a gulch in the desert—
one day they're gushing with water
MSG.16:
From melting ice and snow
cascading out of the mountains,
MSG.17:
But by midsummer they're dry,
gullies baked dry in the sun.
MSG.18:
Travelers who spot them and go out of their way for a drink,
end up in a waterless gulch and die of thirst.
MSG.19:
Merchant caravans from Tema see them and expect water,
tourists from Sheba hope for a cool drink.
MSG.20:
They arrive so confident—but what a disappointment!
They get there, and their faces fall!
MSG.21:
And you, my so-called friends, are no better—
there's nothing to you!
One look at a hard scene and you shrink in fear.
MSG.22:
It's not as though I asked you for anything—
I didn't ask you for one red cent—
MSG.23:
Nor did I beg you to go out on a limb for me.
So why all this dodging and shuffling?
MSG.24:
"Confront me with the truth and I'll shut up,
show me where I've gone off the track.
MSG.25:
Honest words never hurt anyone,
but what's the point of all this pious bluster?
MSG.26:
You pretend to tell me what's wrong with my life,
but treat my words of anguish as so much hot air.
MSG.27:
Are people mere things to you?
Are friends just items of profit and loss?
MSG.28:
"Look me in the eyes!
Do you think I'd lie to your face?
MSG.29:
Think it over—no double-talk!
Think carefully—my integrity is on the line!
MSG.30:
Can you detect anything false in what I say?
Don't you trust me to discern good from evil?

NIV.2:
“If only my anguish could be weighed
and all my misery be placed on the scales!
NIV.3:
It would surely outweigh the sand of the seas—
no wonder my words have been impetuous.
NIV.4:
The arrows of the Almighty are in me,
my spirit drinks in their poison;
God’s terrors are marshaled against me.
NIV.5:
Does a wild donkey bray when it has grass,
or an ox bellow when it has fodder?
NIV.6:
Is tasteless food eaten without salt,
or is there flavor in the white of an egg?
NIV.7:
I refuse to touch it;
such food makes me ill.
NIV.8:
“Oh, that I might have my request,
that God would grant what I hope for,
NIV.9:
that God would be willing to crush me,
to let loose his hand and cut me off!
NIV.10:
Then I would still have this consolation—
my joy in unrelenting pain—
that I had not denied the words of the Holy One.
NIV.11:
“What strength do I have, that I should still hope?
What prospects, that I should be patient?
NIV.12:
Do I have the strength of stone?
Is my flesh bronze?
NIV.13:
Do I have any power to help myself,
now that success has been driven from me?
NIV.14:
“A despairing man should have the devotion of his friends,
even though he forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
NIV.15:
But my brothers are as undependable as intermittent streams,
as the streams that overflow
NIV.16:
when darkened by thawing ice
and swollen with melting snow,
NIV.17:
but that cease to flow in the dry season,
and in the heat vanish from their channels.
NIV.18:
Caravans turn aside from their routes;
they go up into the wasteland and perish.
NIV.19:
The caravans of Tema look for water,
the traveling merchants of Sheba look in hope.
NIV.20:
They are distressed, because they had been confident;
they arrive there, only to be disappointed.
NIV.21:
Now you too have proved to be of no help;
you see something dreadful and are afraid.
NIV.22:
Have I ever said, ‘Give something on my behalf,
pay a ransom for me from your wealth,
NIV.23:
deliver me from the hand of the enemy,
ransom me from the clutches of the ruthless’?
NIV.24:
“Teach me, and I will be quiet;
show me where I have been wrong.
NIV.25:
How painful are honest words!
But what do your arguments prove?
NIV.26:
Do you mean to correct what I say,
and treat the words of a despairing man as wind?
NIV.27:
You would even cast lots for the fatherless
and barter away your friend.
NIV.28:
“But now be so kind as to look at me.
Would I lie to your face?
NIV.29:
Relent, do not be unjust;
reconsider, for my integrity is at stake.
NIV.30:
Is there any wickedness on my lips?
Can my mouth not discern malice?

NRSVCE.2:
“O that my vexation were weighed,
and all my calamity laid in the balances!
NRSVCE.3:
For then it would be heavier than the sand of the sea;
therefore my words have been rash.
NRSVCE.4:
For the arrows of the Almighty are in me;
my spirit drinks their poison;
the terrors of God are arrayed against me.
NRSVCE.5:
Does the wild ass bray over its grass,
or the ox low over its fodder?
NRSVCE.6:
Can that which is tasteless be eaten without salt,
or is there any flavor in the juice of mallows?
NRSVCE.7:
My appetite refuses to touch them;
they are like food that is loathsome to me.
NRSVCE.8:
“O that I might have my request,
and that God would grant my desire;
NRSVCE.9:
that it would please God to crush me,
that he would let loose his hand and cut me off!
NRSVCE.10:
This would be my consolation;
I would even exult in unrelenting pain;
for I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
NRSVCE.11:
What is my strength, that I should wait?
And what is my end, that I should be patient?
NRSVCE.12:
Is my strength the strength of stones,
or is my flesh bronze?
NRSVCE.13:
In truth I have no help in me,
and any resource is driven from me.
NRSVCE.14:
“Those who withhold kindness from a friend
forsake the fear of the Almighty.
NRSVCE.15:
My companions are treacherous like a torrent-bed,
like freshets that pass away,
NRSVCE.16:
that run dark with ice,
turbid with melting snow.
NRSVCE.17:
In time of heat they disappear;
when it is hot, they vanish from their place.
NRSVCE.18:
The caravans turn aside from their course;
they go up into the waste, and perish.
NRSVCE.19:
The caravans of Tema look,
the travelers of Sheba hope.
NRSVCE.20:
They are disappointed because they were confident;
they come there and are confounded.
NRSVCE.21:
Such you have now become to me;
you see my calamity, and are afraid.
NRSVCE.22:
Have I said, ‘Make me a gift’?
Or, ‘From your wealth offer a bribe for me’?
NRSVCE.23:
Or, ‘Save me from an opponent’s hand’?
Or, ‘Ransom me from the hand of oppressors’?
NRSVCE.24:
“Teach me, and I will be silent;
make me understand how I have gone wrong.
NRSVCE.25:
How forceful are honest words!
But your reproof, what does it reprove?
NRSVCE.26:
Do you think that you can reprove words,
as if the speech of the desperate were wind?
NRSVCE.27:
You would even cast lots over the orphan,
and bargain over your friend.
NRSVCE.28:
“But now, be pleased to look at me;
for I will not lie to your face.
NRSVCE.29:
Turn, I pray, let no wrong be done.
Turn now, my vindication is at stake.
NRSVCE.30:
Is there any wrong on my tongue?
Cannot my taste discern calamity?

NET.2: “Oh, if only my grief could be weighed, and my misfortune laid on the scales too!
NET.3: But because it is heavier than the sand of the sea, that is why my words have been wild.
NET.4: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me; my spirit drinks their poison; God’s sudden terrors are arrayed against me.
NET.5: “Does the wild donkey bray when it is near grass? Or does the ox low near its fodder?
NET.6: Can food that is tasteless be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?
NET.7: I have refused to touch such things; they are like loathsome food to me.
NET.8: “Oh that my request would be realized, and that God would grant me what I long for!
NET.9: And that God would be willing to crush me, that he would let loose his hand and kill me.
NET.10: Then I would yet have my comfort, then I would rejoice, in spite of pitiless pain, for I have not concealed the words of the Holy One.
NET.11: What is my strength, that I should wait? and what is my end, that I should prolong my life?
NET.12: Is my strength like that of stones? or is my flesh made of bronze?
NET.13: Is not my power to help myself nothing, and has not every resource been driven from me?
NET.14: “To the one in despair, kindness should come from his friend even if he forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
NET.15: My brothers have been as treacherous as a seasonal stream, and as the riverbeds of the intermittent streams that flow away.
NET.16: They are dark because of ice; snow is piled up over them.
NET.17: When they are scorched, they dry up, when it is hot, they vanish from their place.
NET.18: Caravans turn aside from their routes; they go into the wasteland and perish.
NET.19: The caravans of Tema looked intently for these streams; the traveling merchants of Sheba hoped for them.
NET.20: They were distressed, because each one had been so confident; they arrived there, but were disappointed.
NET.21: For now you have become like these streams that are no help; you see a terror, and are afraid.
NET.22: “Have I ever said, ‘Give me something, and from your fortune make gifts in my favor’?
NET.23: Or ‘Deliver me from the enemy’s power, and from the hand of tyrants ransom me’?
NET.24: “Teach me and I, for my part, will be silent; explain to me how I have been mistaken.
NET.25: How painful are honest words! But what does your reproof prove?
NET.26: Do you intend to criticize mere words, and treat the words of a despairing man as wind?
NET.27: Yes, you would gamble for the fatherless, and auction off your friend.
NET.28: “Now then, be good enough to look at me; and I will not lie to your face!
NET.29: Relent, let there be no falsehood; reconsider, for my righteousness is intact!
NET.30: Is there any falsehood on my lips? Can my mouth not discern evil things?
